payload.title: _predecessor_rejection still entity-encodes < and > into the sealed refusal row at mint, and from prompt v8 untrusted_block encodes the result again, so a refused answer's quoted '<' reaches the successor agent as '&lt;' and cannot be told apart from an original literal '<'
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/agent_invocations.py:1115-1121 (the mint-time second escaper: replace('<', '<') and replace('>', '>') on every rejection reason)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/agent_invocations.py:1125-1128 (each reason is cut to 400 characters AFTER the encoding, so the cut can land inside an entity)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/agent_invocations.py:1268-1272 (v8 renders the predecessor block through _untrusted_section, the owner's escape)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/text_safety.py:79 (the owner encodes '&' first, then '<' and '>')
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/agent_invocations.py:1962-1971 (every fresh mint stamps the current version v8 and attaches the pre-escaped row, so the mint-time escape serves no version any more)
aria-kernel/tests/test_trust_boundary_f40b.py:367-373 (the predecessor test checks only that the injected text stays inside the block; no test pins a single encoding layer for a plain '<')
payload.rule_violated: Single owner per fact (text_safety.untrusted_block is the one escaper of untrusted prompt data, PLAN-v2 F4.0b; an escape stored in a sealed row is a second owner with no pin).
payload.notes: A refused answer whose rejection reason quotes a ref such as Map<string, Foo> is sealed as Map<string, Foo> when the successor is minted. The v8 prompt renders that body through untrusted_block, which encodes the '&' again, so the successor reads Map&lt;string, Foo&gt;. The v8 data notice says one decode turns < into '<', so the agent decodes to the text '<' and not to the generic it was refused for, and the original '<' and an original literal '<' render identically. The 400-character cut after encoding can also split an entity and the owner then encodes its '&'. No boundary is breached; the fidelity of the refusal the successor is told to avoid repeating is lost. Close condition: Store the raw reason in _predecessor_rejection (slice the raw text, no replace) and let untrusted_block be the only escaper; rows already sealed keep their bytes and render under their own version. Add a mint-then-render test in test_trust_boundary_f40b.py: a reason with a plain '<' renders as < exactly once and a reason holding a literal '<' renders as &lt;. Verified at origin/main ae2958653d.
